rewrites.blindSummary:
No criminal exposure: its own legislature decriminalised same-sex conduct in the 1979 code revision (effective 1980), age of consent equal at 16. No local protections of practical substance exist: nothing criminalises a trans visitor, and next to nothing shields one.

Partner travel is the sharpest edge. Marriages performed elsewhere must be recognised under a 2022 national statute, yet the state performs none: officials long treated the 2015 national ruling as 'under review', a judge said in 2016 he would not apply it, and licences remain withheld through 2024-26 — a 2026 review concludes any same-sex applicant must be served, but none has applied, so spousal recognition is untested.

Social climate is conservative and church-centred, reserved behaviour expected; yet it is the homeland of a widely accepted indigenous third-gender presence; trans-presenting travellers more often meet cultural familiarity than the hostility recorded in some neighbouring state. Net: low state risk, thin institutional cover, reliance on informal tolerance.
rewrites.blindTangential:
Applicability of the 2015 national marriage-ruling remains formally unsettled — the top government lawyer said in 2015 it was 'still being reviewed'; a district-court judge confirmed in 2016 he had not read it and would not perform such weddings absent local law change. A 2026 practitioners' review argues the ruling binds, but reaching that conclusion runs through local courts and then the national department overseeing this province — a path no one has taken.

Nothing newer than 2024-26: no post-2024 local ruling, law or incident touching trans people was located, and a 2024 local legal survey still treats the local marriage restriction as operative and its constitutional durability as open.
rewrites.blindLocalsOnly:
Residents raised male, embodying both genders, are documented as integral to traditional family life; a society formed in 2010 as explicit cultural reclamation, and witnesses themselves opposed the marriage bill on cultural and religious grounds at a 2003 legislature hearing. Birth-record gender markers change only with medical documentation; plain corrections are limited to record errors.

A 2024 local survey by a visiting constitutional-law professor tested whether the marriage ban would survive a constitutional challenge, framing local culture in collectivist terms — a residents' and scholars' debate with little direct visitor stake.
rewrites.blindOutOfScope: Passport 'X' marker availability for nationals of the parent nation is unverified. No trans-specific incident or enforcement episode for 2024-26 was found; absence of evidence is not safety. Comparative-ranking language is out of scope for this record.
blindSourceSummaries: Academic research guide on regional gender identities (updated 2026-07-23): records a third-gender society formed in 2010 by merging two associations, explicitly re-anchored to cultural pride; defines the role as born male but embodying both male and female traits, 'a recognized and integral part of traditional culture'; historic suppression followed by contemporary reclaiming.

Travel column (2009-07-01) answering a honeymoon question about this state: the two neighbouring nations share the chiefly family system; ~57,000 residents; 'culture tends toward traditionalism, and reserved behavior by people of all orientations is expected'; homosexuality a widely accepted part of the local culture, unlike the homophobia recorded in one neighbouring nation; indigenous third-gender locals reportedly court Western gay men; a local artist calls the place 'the homeland of' third-gender culture; hotels skew business-travel.

News report (2015-07-10): this state was the only part of the parent nation unsure whether the 2015 national marriage ruling applied — the top government lawyer: 'We're still reviewing the decision to determine its applicability... I don't know', while other states under the same parent nation moved to apply it. ~50,000 residents, conservative Christian society, motto invoking God first; third-gender tradition noted; a prominent figure says many traditional-role advocates don't push marriage out of respect for culture/religion, yet would herself be first to apply; no marriage applications had been made; local-law experts said recognition required voluntary adoption or litigation, warning the review had a chilling effect.

The legislature's upper chamber voted down a bill that would have outlawed same-sex marriage in March 2003, after a committee recommended the bill be killed; the bill sought to preempt the kind of marriage lawsuits then unfolding in parent-nation states. At the committee hearing a third-gender resident testified that such locals 'don't believe in marriages with other men', describing them as men expressing femininity through dress and speech who do not seek same-sex marriage, citing a religious upbringing. For this record: the state deliberately declined a formal marriage ban before the 2015 national ruling, with contemporaneous local voices on the question.

In January 2016 the legislature's upper chamber unanimously confirmed the former top government lawyer as a district-court judge, filling a retiring seat. At the confirmation hearing a retired associate judge of the final local court asked whether he had read the 2015 national ruling; he replied he had not read it and that his court 'doesn't deal with this ruling', and said he would not perform weddings for same-sex couples unless local laws are changed. For this record: direct evidence that eighteen months after the national ruling the local judiciary was operating on the premise it did not automatically apply, with named actors and dates.

2026 law review article by two attorneys practising in this state (local legal aid, with a freedom-from-religion foundation) concluding that the 2015 national ruling DOES apply despite local officials' statements, and that the state would have to issue a marriage certificate to any same-sex couple that applied. Records that to date no couple has applied for a licence, and lays out the litigation roadmap: the final local court first (defendant the registry officer), then the parent nation's interior department. For this record: the freshest dated authority on the exact open question (is the 2015 ruling operative?), separating the law from the practical reality (no licences sought/issued).

Reported July 2024: a local survey by a visiting constitutional and comparative law professor testing whether the state's same-sex marriage ban would survive a constitutional challenge, also probing cultural dimensions bearing on the question (collectivistic vs individualistic orientation; linear vs polychronic time). For this record: as of mid-2024, nine years after the national ruling and more than a year after the 2022 national statute obliged recognition of outside marriages (Dec 13 2022), the local ban is treated on-site as operative and its constitutional durability as an open question.
